Kim / Markus —

Quick summary: OmniWell is asking for a 60% discount off list for a 6-month pilot of our hosted API (chat + embeddings) to validate care-path summarization across 30 clinics. They want a single-line commercial (no seat limits) and an onboarding discount plus waived integration professional fees. Attached: omniwell_proposal_v4.pdf (proposal + SOW stub).

Why I’m escalating: the requested discount and waiver exceed our standard pilot guardrails (max 40% for this SKU, professional-services must be billed or offset). Customer is mid-market but strategic given their channel relationships. I need an approval path (VP/CFO) for:
- 60% discount on hosted usage for 6 months
- waive $25k integration fee
- commit to an 18-month expansion MOU (verbal; TBD) in exchange for the discount

Ask: can we get quick commercial sign-off or do we counter to 40% + $10k onboarding? Candidate concessions I can live with: a capped timebox (60% only for first 60 days), minimum monthly usage floor, or milestone-based payments.

Jordan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Kim / Jordan —

Reviewed omniwell_proposal_v4 and ran a quick commercial P&L based on Jordan's usage estimates (chat-forward with embeddings). Key points:
- Baseline expected pilot consumption: ~1.2M tokens / month (model mix: 50% chat gpt-like gen, 50% embeddings).
- Estimated variable cost to Redwood (GPU cycles + infra) at our Hosted rate: ~$6k/month for the pilot (unoptimized).
- List price revenue at 40% discount yields positive contribution margin (~35% contribution) at the pilot scale.
- At 60% discount + waived $25k onboarding, we run contribution negative (~-12%) unless there is a binding expansion commitment (signed MOU) to 18 months with guaranteed minimums (~$18k/month average after expansion).

Recommendation: We should not approve an unconditional 60% discount. Approveable options that limit downside:
A) 40% pilot discount + $5k onboarding credit + 6-month minimum usage floor (preferred).
B) Timeboxed 60% discount for first 60 days only, then revert to 40% for the remainder of pilot; require milestone payments (25% upfront) and a signed 18-month MOU that includes a minimum blended spend floor.
C) If Marissa wants to make a precedent-setting exception (not recommended), require CFO-level carveout with explicit loss allowance and documented success criteria plus escrowed milestone payments.

Attached: commercial_review_notes.md (spreadsheet notes: sensitivity analysis).

If you want, I can draft a one-page memo for Marissa summarizing financial impact and precedent risk.

Markus Klein
Finance Director, Commercial Operations

Attachment: commercial_review_notes.md (analysis summary)

Subject: Exec sign-off request: OmniWell pilot discount exception (DEAL-OMW-2027-034)

Marissa —

Short ask: permission to grant a commercial exception for OmniWell Health to close a time-sensitive pilot. They are requesting a 60% discount + waived $25k onboarding fee. After review, Markus and I recommend the following approvable path:

Proposal (recommended):
- 40% discount for the 6-month pilot
- $5k onboarding credit applied to first invoice
- 6-month minimum usage floor (see commercial_review_notes.md for thresholds)
- Delivery milestone schedule in SOW and 25% upfront payment
- Clear expansion MOU language (18-month target) and channel non-exclusivity

If you prefer a more aggressive concession to secure the deal immediately, alternative (conditional): 60% discount timeboxed to first 60 days only, conditional on 25% upfront payment and a signed MOU that commits to minimum spend thereafter — this requires CFO sign-off of the negative contribution allowance.

Why approve? OmniWell is a channel-forward customer with potential to expand to 300 clinics; they have references that could accelerate three small strategic buys in Q3. Why not approve straight 60%? It creates a negative-contribution precedent and expands the aisle of discounting for similar mid-market healthcare prospects.
